entries.summary: Bearish elevated downside-risk bias retained after confirmed Nvidia CEO transition. Reuters recorded Nasdaq Composite -1.47% at Thursday's opening print, validating an initial cash-market decline, while Reuters separately reported Nvidia down more than 12% intraday. These are not synchronized 10:30 ET readings; live SOX/QQQ, breadth, VXN/VIX and matching Treasury quotes remain unavailable. No additional material three-session bias change beyond the prior 10:28 ET assessment.
bullish: Nvidia's official statement confirms interim CEO Colette Kress and new board chair Harvey Jones, providing a transition framework.
Prior curated Siemens and Foxconn AI infrastructure demand evidence remains constructive for longer-term sector fundamentals.
A verified SOX relative-strength recovery, improving breadth and contained volatility could reverse the downside path.
bearish: Nasdaq Composite opened -1.47% on November 12 per Reuters, an actual cash-market response to the Nvidia transition.
Reuters reports Nvidia down more than 12% intraday; leadership and policy uncertainty can propagate to AI suppliers and financing.
Hotter-than-expected Friday PPI, higher yields or renewed Fed-hike repricing could exacerbate technology selling.

editorial.marketOverview: The three-session outlook remains bearish with elevated downside risk after Nvidia's official announcement that Jensen Huang resigned and Colette Kress became interim CEO. The company also named Harvey Jones board chair. Reuters reported the Nasdaq Composite opening 1.47% lower on November 12, establishing an actual cash-session reaction beyond the earlier futures indications. Reuters separately described Nvidia shares falling more than 12% intraday. These observations are asynchronous and do not establish current QQQ/SOX breadth or volatility confirmation.
editorial.whatChanged: Compared with the 10:28 EST snapshot, the important incremental evidence is the Reuters-confirmed -1.47% Nasdaq Composite opening print and an intraday Nvidia decline greater than 12%. The CEO transition was already incorporated into the preceding material bearish downgrade, so the new observations strengthen rather than change the directional scenario. The curated Open Watch file still shows 159 events, updated 11:25 UTC; it has not independently supplied a new post-transition catalyst.
editorial.marketInterpretation: The cash-market opening decline supports the thesis that leadership uncertainty is being repriced across technology, but the absence of synchronized SOX, QQQ, VXN/VIX and breadth prevents claims of a confirmed broad semiconductor breakdown. Nvidia's leadership and chip-export uncertainty is the immediate risk, while Siemens and Foxconn demand reports are longer-horizon fundamental counterweights. Historical November 10 Treasury yields of 4.988% for 10Y and 4.731% for 2Y imply +25.7 basis points, not a scaled yield of hundreds of percent. Secondary rounded November 12 indications imply +23 bp but are not matched live quotes. Earlier Brent $91.29 and WTI $85.29 at 04:26 UTC are stale; FedWatch probabilities are also historical.
editorial.threeDayPath: Thursday November 12 is the initial leadership-transition cash-market price-discovery session; a lower Nasdaq opening is now verified, but the closing breadth and SOX response remain decisive. Friday November 13's 08:30 EST October PPI could reinforce or ease rate-sensitive selling. Monday November 16 tests whether the weakness persists across semiconductor leadership and market breadth or begins to reverse. This is a conditional scenario, not a forecast of exact returns.
editorial.bullCase: A credible succession process under interim CEO Colette Kress and board chair Harvey Jones could stabilize customer and employee confidence. AI data-center orders reported by Siemens and Foxconn suggest underlying demand has not vanished. A verified improvement in SOX relative to QQQ, positive breadth, stable yields and falling VXN/VIX would weaken the bearish thesis.
editorial.bearCase: Founder-CEO departure, uncertain policy relationships and potential AI ecosystem financing spillovers could extend de-risking beyond Nvidia. Nasdaq's 1.47% lower opening and Nvidia's reported intraday decline greater than 12% are initial supporting evidence. Weak SOX participation, worsening breadth, rising volatility and a hotter Friday PPI would compound the risk.
